name: Bilingual English–French work (category)
summary: Using English–French bilingualism for translation, interpretation, localization review, tutoring or bilingual service work — a distinctly Canadian advantage with an earnings premium that is strongest in Quebec.
whatYouDo: Depending on the route: translating or revising documents, interpreting calls or meetings, reviewing French-Canadian content or voices for AI and localization companies, tutoring French, or serving clients in both languages. Professional translation and interpretation usually need training or accreditation; some task-based fr-CA work needs only native fluency.
appeal: Job Bank national median for translators, terminologists and interpreters about $33.95/hour (range $20–$51)
The federal Translation Bureau buys freelance linguistic services through supply arrangements and a supplier directory
Research reports a bilingual earnings premium, largest in Quebec
Global companies specifically recruit Canadian French speakers (e.g. CrowdGen fr-CA voice tasks, Welocalize French Canadian linguists; LanguageLine added French Canadian video interpreting)
watchOuts: Outside Quebec, studies find the wage premium smaller or absent once occupation is accounted for
Translation Bureau supply arrangements or directory registration do not guarantee any work
Professional routes typically require training, certification or accreditation exams
Several 'French' postings found were for France- or US-based roles; check for fr-CA and location rules

credentials: Translation training or certification often expected for professional translation
Accreditation exams for Translation Bureau interpretation

training.notes: Formal translation training/certification helps for professional routes; costs not researched.

compensation.notes: Job Bank wages for Translators, terminologists and interpreters (NOC 51114), 2023–2024 LFS, updated Nov 2025: national median $33.95; Quebec median $36.26, Ontario $25.64. Employee-oriented data; freelance and task rates differ.

reliability.notes: Varies by route; federal supplier status carries no work guarantee; task platforms are sporadic.

applicationSteps: Assess your written and spoken level in both languages
Pick a route: fr-CA task platforms, tutoring, localization vendors, or professional translation/interpretation
For federal work, review the Translation Bureau's supplier routes (supply arrangement or directory; CRA business number and procurement business number needed)
Consider formal training or certification for professional translation
fitsIf: You read, write and speak both English and French well and want to turn that into income, especially in or near Quebec, Ottawa or New Brunswick.
notFitIf: Your French (or English) is conversational only, without strong writing skills.

sources.title: English-French bilingualism advantages at work
sources.notes: Reports a 2019 Conference Board of Canada study: outside Quebec, bilinguals are about one-fifth of the workforce and more likely to have higher incomes and lower unemployment.

sources.title: Bilingualism Translates into Higher Earnings, Study Finds
sources.publisher: University of Guelph, Lang School of Business
sources.notes: University news item on a study linking bilingualism to higher earnings. Search summary cites Christofides & Swidinsky (2001 Census): bilingual men +3.6%, women +6.6% vs English-only (attribution to this page not certain).
